history.content: Hi, my phone has no service at all—no bars, nothing loads, and I can't send picture messages. Can you help?

I can help you with this issue. To begin, I need to identify your account. Could you please provide either your phone number, customer ID, or your full name along with your date of birth? This will allow me to check your line status and assist you further.
My phone number is +1-617-555-0148 and my name is Sofia Martinez. Would you like my date of birth as well?

Thank you for providing your information. Your line status is currently "Active," which means there are no suspensions or contract issues on your account.

To help resolve your "no service" and picture messaging (MMS) issues, I’ll guide you through some troubleshooting steps. Could you please confirm if you are able to check your phone’s status bar and perform some actions if needed? This will help us quickly identify the cause of the problem.
Yes, I can check my phone’s status bar and perform actions if you need me to. Just let me know what to do next.

Great! Let’s start by checking your phone’s status bar to see if there are any indicators that can help us diagnose the issue.

Please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- Is Airplane Mode enabled (look for an airplane icon)?
- What is the signal strength (are there any bars, or does it show “No Service” or “No Signal”)?
- Do you see any network type indicators (like 5G, 4G, LTE, etc.)?
- Is mobile data enabled (look for a data icon or similar indicator)?

If you’re unsure about any of these, let me know what you see, and I’ll guide you further.
I see the airplane mode icon, it says 'No Signal,' and data is enabled. My battery is at 87%.

Thank you for the details. Since Airplane Mode is enabled, this will disable all wireless connections, including cellular service and mobile data. That’s why you’re seeing “No Signal” and are unable to send picture messages.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. Once you do that, wait a few seconds and check if your signal bars return and if you regain service. Let me know what you see after turning off Airplane Mode.
Airplane mode is now OFF, but I still don't have any signal bars and it still says 'No Service.' What should I do next?

Thank you for turning off Airplane Mode. Since you still have no signal, the next step is to check your SIM card status, as issues with the SIM card can also cause a complete loss of service.

Please check your SIM card status on your phone. If you see any messages such as “SIM missing,” “SIM not detected,” or “SIM locked,” let me know. If you’re not sure how to check, let me know what your phone displays regarding the SIM card, or if you see any related notifications.

If you see an option to reseat or reinsert your SIM card, please try that as well and let me know if anything changes.
I checked the SIM card status and it says 'SIM not detected.' I can try reseating the SIM card if you want.

Yes, please go ahead and reseat your SIM card. This means removing the SIM card from your phone and then carefully reinserting it to ensure it’s properly seated.

After you’ve done this, wait a few moments and check if your phone now detects the SIM card and if you regain any signal bars. Let me know what happens after you reseat the SIM card.
After reseating the SIM card, it now says the SIM status is active, but I still have no signal bars and it still shows 'No Service.' What should I do next?

Thank you for reseating your SIM card. Since your SIM status is now active but you still have no signal, the next step is to check your phone’s network settings, specifically the Access Point Name (APN) settings, as incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from connecting to the network.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if anything looks incorrect or if there is no APN set. If you’re unsure, let me know what you see for the APN name and MMSC URL, or if you see any error messages.
My APN settings show 'fast.telecom.net' and the status says they're correct, with the MMSC URL set to 'http://mms.telecom.net/mms/wapenc.' What should I try next?

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Since your SIM is active and your APN settings are correct, but you still have no signal, the next step is to reboot your device. Sometimes, a simple restart can help your phone reconnect to the network after changes like reseating the SIM card.

Please restart (reboot) your phone now. After it powers back on, check if you have any signal bars or service. Let me know the result after the reboot.
My phone rebooted successfully, but I still don't have any signal bars and it still says 'No Service.' What else should I try?

Thank you for following all the steps so far. Since your SIM is now detected, APN settings are correct, Airplane Mode is off, and you’ve rebooted your device but still have no signal, this suggests a deeper network or hardware issue that cannot be resolved through standard troubleshooting.

At this point, I will transfer you to a human agent who can further investigate and assist you with your service issue.

YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.
